speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a pruritic rash on your bilateral upper extremities; to begin my assessment, how long has this rash been present, and have you noticed any specific triggers like new soaps, plants, or foods?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text: That duration of five months with intermittent worsening is concerning for a chronic etiology. Have you noticed any changes in your nails, scalp, or the lining of your elbows, and does the rash become more intense after a hot shower or during the night?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities. I also have No fever, No joint pains, No recent illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming those negative findings. Given the chronic, intermittent nature of this pruritic rash on your upper extremities without systemic symptoms, is there any history of atopic disease (like asthma or eczema), or does the rash appear more pronounced in areas exposed to friction or sunlight?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No history of serious illness. No known drug allergies. Takes no medications. Social history: College student studying graphic design. Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. No recreational drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Allergic Contact Dermatitis (specifically from henna tattoo ink), though chronic urticaria or early psoriasis remain differentials pending visual confirmation. REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide a clear photograph of the rash distribution on your upper extremities.
